definition: A function that converts a vector of raw scores into a probability distribution, where all values are positive and sum to one.
details: Softmax is used throughout neural networks, including in attention mechanisms to normalize attention scores and in output layers to convert logits into a probability distribution over possible tokens or classes.

explainer.lead: The softmax function turns a vector of raw scores into a probability distribution with positive values that sum to one. It is used throughout neural networks to convert scores into usable probabilities.

tiers.eli5: It takes a list of scores and turns them into percentages that add up to 100, so you can read them as chances.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply softmax to attention scores to normalize them and to output logits to get a distribution over tokens or classes. A common pitfall is numerical overflow with large scores, so implementations subtract the maximum before exponentiating.
tiers.paperLevel: Softmax maps a vector of raw scores to a probability distribution in which all values are positive and sum to one. It is used in attention mechanisms to normalize attention scores and in output layers to convert logits into a distribution over tokens or classes.

explainer.example: A classifier outputs raw scores for three classes; softmax converts them into three positive probabilities that sum to one, and the largest probability is read as the predicted class.
